finding.claim: The /invoice/<inv_id> route returns any invoice by ID with no authentication or ownership check (IDOR / broken access control). The sibling /my/invoice route does enforce ownership, which shows the check was intended here.
finding.source: inv_id URL path parameter, controlled by any requester
finding.sink: jsonify(inv) returns the full invoice record, including the customer field and any other data in it

trace.note: route /invoice/<inv_id> declared with no auth decorator or before_request hook
INVOICES.get(inv_id) fetches the record by ID alone, with no comparison to g.user
the full record is returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: Searched the file for auth decorators, before_request hooks and any g.user comparison on this route. None exist. The ownership check at line 16 is only in get_my_invoice. The repo is a single file, so no middleware is visible. A global auth hook could exist elsewhere, but it would not provide per-object ownership anyway.

verdict.reason: invoices.py:7-10 serves INVOICES.get(inv_id) via jsonify with no auth decorator, before_request hook, or g.user ownership check (unlike invoices.py:16 in /my/invoice), so any requester can read any invoice by ID.
